value: Do basal forebrain neurons have response fields as complex as their anatomy and cell-type diversity suggest, or does the population act as a relatively undifferentiated group responding to all salient and rewarding stimuli?

Recording large ensembles in rat basal forebrain during a visuospatial attention task, the paper shows the population carries many distinct task-phase-specific firing patterns - including multi-peaked cells and oppositely-tuned counterpart groups - that distinguish every phase of the task, and that the same repertoire of patterns appears in posterior parietal cortex.

quote: In the present work, large ensemble recordings of BF neurons were obtained during performance of a selective attention task with the goal of filling, to some extent, this gap in knowledge.
Among the full population of BF neurons, multiple distinct and complex forms of task-phase-specific activity are realized, forming unique population firing patterns for all task phases.

value: Anatomical organisation of local interconnections and of extrinsic afferents partitions basal forebrain neurons into distinct groups, which is why firing patterns cluster and why pair-wise trial-to-trial variability tracks pattern similarity.
quote: The foregoing results suggest that, for complex behavioral tasks, BF neurons are organized into distinct groups by virtue of the anatomical organization of their local interconnections, by their extrinsic afferents, or both.

value: Whichever subset of basal forebrain neurons is active at a given moment raises responsiveness specifically in the cortical targets those neurons reach, so task-phase-specific firing produces task-phase-specific cortical modulation.
quote: currently active set of BF neurons yields enhanced responsiveness among the subset of efferent targets reached by those neurons.

value: Simultaneous peaks and troughs in GABAergic and glutamatergic basal forebrain neurons could amplify inhibition of the cortical target, because GABAergic drive rises while excitatory glutamatergic drive is withdrawn.
quote: In an admittedly simplistic scenario, for instance, GABA and glutamate neurons could reach simultaneous peaks and troughs in activity, yielding amplification of GABAergic inhibition through coincident disfacilitation of excitatory glutamatergic input.

value: Distinct sub-populations of basal forebrain neurons reached their peak firing rate at every phase of the task, including the pure locomotion period between nose-poke and return to the arena centre, not only at stimulus onset and reward.
quote: First, distinct subsets of BF neurons reach peak activity at each task phase, including, for example, the time period directly between nose-poke and return to the center plate.

value: Nearly every category of task-phase-specific firing had a mirror-image counterpart category whose mean firing pattern was strongly negatively correlated with it, so at each task phase one group of neurons peaked while another fell to a trough.
quote: The mean task-phase-specific firing pattern for nearly every grouping of BF neurons has a counterpart in another grouping for which the mean task-phase-specific pattern is strongly negatively correlated

value: Apart from persistence before the light flash and after reward, no basal forebrain ensemble firing pattern recurred at a later task phase, so each task phase was marked by its own distinct population firing vector.
quote: While persistence in BF ensemble firing patterns is found over the time period preceding light flash onset and after reward obtainment, further evidence for pattern recurrence is not found, directly evidencing the fact that BF networks are capable of generating a large repertoire of distinct firing patterns.

value: Posterior parietal cortex neurons, clustered independently by the same algorithm, produced groups that each had both a strongly matching and a strongly opposing basal forebrain counterpart pattern.
quote: Remarkably, despite independence in the application of the algorithm to the BF and PPC populations, mean rate vectors for nearly all PPC groups had BF counterparts with highly similar and highly dissimilar patterns.

value: During the anticipatory period before the light flash — when attention to the visual field should be highest — basal forebrain mean firing was at its lowest and few neurons peaked, arguing against a role confined to anticipatory attention.
quote: Among the full population of BF neurons, mean activity rates were actually lowest during this time period, and associated with peak activity in only a few neurons.

value: The largest proportion of neurons peaked, and population mean rate was highest, in the period just after the light flash, pointing to a basal forebrain role in initiating and maintaining responses to relevant stimuli.
quote: Instead, the time period just after light flash was associated with peak firing in the largest proportion of neurons as well as the highest mean rate across the full population.
